title: 09 — The Databricks AI Stack
html:
09 — The Databricks AI Stack

The one idea: treat models, prompts and agents like data: version them, govern them in the catalog, evaluate them against a fixed set before release, and trace every call. Retrieval works best as a hybrid of keyword and vector search, with every passage carrying its source page.

1. What it is

Piece Job
MLflow 3 Tracking, the model registry (in Unity Catalog), GenAI tracing, evaluation with LLM judges, and a prompt registry
Model Serving Hosts your own models, Databricks-hosted foundation models (pay-per-token or provisioned throughput) and external models behind one endpoint API
AI Gateway Governance on serving endpoints: rate limits, usage tracking, guardrails, payload logging. Its 2026 status was not confirmed
AI Functions SQL functions that call models: ai_query, ai_extract, ai_classify, ai_parse_document and others
AI Search (formerly Vector Search) Indexes that sync from Delta tables. Vector, keyword (BM25) and hybrid retrieval, with a reranker
Agent Bricks Umbrella for building agents and document-intelligence tasks
Managed MCP servers MCP access to Unity Catalog functions, search indexes and Genie spaces (Public Preview when checked)

2. Why it matters

  • Document-heavy platforms need parsing, extraction and classification at scale, preferably in SQL next to the data.
  • Models change published numbers. They need the same governance, versioning and release discipline as data.
  • Agents need retrieval that cites where an answer came from.

3. The main ideas

3.1 MLflow 3

  • LoggedModel is a first-class entity. It ties an application or model version to its code commit, configuration, traces and evaluation runs.
  • Tracing gives end-to-end visibility for GenAI apps, with automatic instrumentation for many frameworks (per the docs, 20 or more, including OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex and Anthropic).
  • Evaluation: built-in and custom LLM judges, evaluation datasets and production monitoring.
  • Prompt registry: versioned prompts with Unity Catalog integration.
  • Models in Unity Catalog: catalog.schema.model, with versions, aliases (for example @champion), lineage and permissions.

3.2 AI Functions

Function Use
ai_parse_document PDFs, images, Word and PowerPoint to structured text and layout. GA on 16 April 2026 per the release notes. Limits of 500 pages and 100 MB per document
ai_extract Pull named fields from text
ai_classify Assign one of your labels
ai_query Call any serving endpoint with your own prompt or model

Status, checked 2026-10-26: the latest release notes say ai_extract and ai_classify are GA, while older pages still show Public Preview. A third-party guide says AI Functions need serverless SQL warehouses or recent runtimes.

-- Not run: requires a workspace with AI Functions. Paths and labels are made up.
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT path, ai_parse_document(content) AS doc
  FROM READ_FILES('/Volumes/fin/landing/factsheets/', format => 'binaryFile'))
SELECT path,
       ai_classify(CAST(doc AS STRING), ARRAY('factsheet', 'annual_report', 'rating_rationale')) AS doc_type
FROM parsed;

3.3 Retrieval: chunk, index, search, rerank

---
title: Hybrid retrieval with citations
---
flowchart LR
    D["Parsed documents<br/>(page, box, vintage)"] --> CH["Chunk<br/>by section, keep page ids"]
    CH --> IDX["Search index<br/>synced from a Delta table"]
    Q["Question"] --> KW["Keyword search (BM25)"]
    Q --> VS["Vector search (embeddings)"]
    IDX --> KW
    IDX --> VS
    KW --> F["Fuse rankings<br/>(e.g. reciprocal rank fusion)"]
    VS --> F
    F --> RR["Rerank top results"]
    RR --> A["Answer with citations:<br/>document, page, vintage"]
  • Chunking: split by document structure (sections, tables), not fixed character counts. Keep the page number and vintage on every chunk.
  • Keyword (BM25) finds exact terms, tickers, ISINs and abbreviations. Vector search finds paraphrases. Hybrid gets both.
  • In Databricks AI Search, query_type="hybrid" turns on hybrid search (up to 200 results). The reranker became GA in December 2025. Full-text-only search was in Beta.

3.4 Serving and GPUs

  • Custom model endpoints scale to zero, or stay warm for latency. GPU types depend on region.
  • Foundation Model APIs: pay-per-token for experiments, provisioned throughput for production guarantees.
  • External models: route to outside providers through the same endpoint and governance. Redact before anything leaves your boundary.

4. Working code

The script ranks five made-up chunks with BM25 and with a toy vector similarity, then fuses the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion. Standard library only. The "embedding" is a tiny synonym table standing in for a real embedding model.

import math, re
from collections import Counter

# Chunks from made-up documents, each carrying the page and vintage it came from.
chunks = [
    {"id": "c1", "page": 4,  "text": "The total expense ratio of the direct plan is 0.62 percent."},
    {"id": "c2", "page": 9,  "text": "Expenses charged to the scheme are within the regulatory limit."},
    {"id": "c3", "page": 12, "text": "The rating outlook was revised to negative due to rising leverage."},
    {"id": "c4", "page": 2,  "text": "TER for the regular plan stands at 1.05 percent of daily net assets."},
    {"id": "c5", "page": 7,  "text": "Net asset value rose 3 percent over the quarter."},
]
tok = lambda s: re.findall(r"[a-z0-9.]+", s.lower())

# Keyword side: BM25, the standard ranking formula behind most full-text search.
docs = [tok(c["text"]) for c in chunks]
avgdl = sum(map(len, docs)) / len(docs)
df = Counter(t for d in docs for t in set(d))
def bm25(query, k1=1.2, b=0.75):
    scores = []
    for c, d in zip(chunks, docs):
        tf = Counter(d)
        s = sum(math.log(1 + (len(docs) - df[t] + 0.5) / (df[t] + 0.5)) *
                tf[t] * (k1 + 1) / (tf[t] + k1 * (1 - b + b * len(d) / avgdl)) for t in tok(query) if t in tf)
        scores.append((s, c["id"]))
    return [cid for s, cid in sorted(scores, reverse=True) if s > 0]

# Vector side: a toy "embedding" that knows a few synonyms, standing in for a real embedding model.
SYN = {"ter": "expense", "expenses": "expense", "expense": "expense", "ratio": "expense", "fee": "expense",
       "charged": "expense", "nav": "value", "value": "value"}
def embed(text):
    return Counter(SYN.get(t, t) for t in tok(text))
def cosine(a, b):
    dot = sum(a[k] * b[k] for k in a)
    return dot / (math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in a.values())) * math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in b.values())) or 1)
def vector(query):
    q = embed(query)
    return [c["id"] for s, c in sorted(((cosine(q, embed(c["text"])), c) for c in chunks),
                                       key=lambda x: -x[0]) if s > 0]

# Reciprocal rank fusion: combine rankings without comparing their incompatible scores.
def rrf(*rankings, k=60):
    score = Counter()
    for ranking in rankings:
        for rank, cid in enumerate(ranking, start=1):
            score[cid] += 1 / (k + rank)
    return [cid for cid, _ in score.most_common()]

query = "TER fee of the plan"
kw, vec = bm25(query), vector(query)
fused = rrf(kw, vec)
print("keyword (BM25):", kw)
print("vector        :", vec)
print("hybrid (RRF)  :", fused)
top = next(c for c in chunks if c["id"] == fused[0])
print(f"Top answer cites page {top['page']}: {top['text']}")

Output:

keyword (BM25): ['c4', 'c1', 'c2', 'c5', 'c3']
vector        : ['c1', 'c2', 'c4', 'c5', 'c3']
hybrid (RRF)  : ['c1', 'c4', 'c2', 'c5', 'c3']
Top answer cites page 4: The total expense ratio of the direct plan is 0.62 percent.

What to notice:

  • BM25 ranks c4 first, because "TER" appears literally. It also scores c2 and c5 on common words like "of" and "the", which is why real systems use stop-word handling and analysers.
  • Vector search ranks c1 first, because "expense ratio" means the same as "TER fee".
  • RRF puts the two best chunks on top, without having to compare BM25 scores with cosine scores. The answer carries its page number.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Vector-only retrieval for financial text. It misses exact identifiers and abbreviations. Use hybrid.
  2. Chunks without page and vintage. Answers can't be cited or checked.
  3. Evaluating with a moving test set. Freeze the evaluation dataset per release.
  4. Calling external models with raw documents. Redact first, and route through governed endpoints.
  5. Unversioned prompts. Prompts change behaviour like code. Version them in the registry.

6. Exercise (1.5 hours)

  1. Add a "regular plan versus direct plan" question to the script and see which side (keyword or vector) gets it right.
  2. Change RRF's k from 60 to 1 and explain how the fused ranking moves.
  3. On Free Edition, run ai_parse_document on one made-up PDF in a volume, and store the output with the file path and page numbers.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What does MLflow 3's LoggedModel connect together?
  2. Why does hybrid retrieval beat either side alone for financial documents?
  3. Why use reciprocal rank fusion instead of adding scores?
  4. What are the documented limits of ai_parse_document?
  5. What must every chunk carry for answers to be checkable?

Answers

  1. A model or application version, with its code commit, configuration, traces and evaluation runs.
  2. Keyword search catches exact ids and abbreviations, and vector search catches paraphrases. Financial questions need both.
  3. BM25 and cosine scores are on different scales. RRF combines ranks, which are comparable.
  4. 500 pages and 100 MB per document.
  5. Its document, page (or box) and vintage.
